title: Intel | Questions to be ready for
purpose: Separate two-page speaking preparation. Suggested first-person answers; the author should understand and be able to explain each calculation. Not a submission appendix or a substitute for original interviews.

opening.heading: 60-second opening
opening.text: My recommendation is a modest-conviction relative short of Intel. I allow a strong recovery: 2027 server CPU revenue grows 44%, and operating profit totals $111 billion over 2027–2030. The question is what shareholders keep after paying for that recovery. My model produces $28 billion of economic owner cash over those four years. The valuation then depends heavily on how long premium margins last and how efficiently new capacity earns revenue. The strongest challenge to my case is simple: a roughly 39.3% mature DCAI margin can cover the reference price if risk declines as assumed. My central 2030 value is also above entry, so this requires a portfolio argument. The illustrated position returns 6.43% annually under selected assumptions, but 4.91% under a consistent alternative method. That limits my conviction.

questions_and_answers.question: Why short a stock your model values at $70.98 in 2030?
questions_and_answers.answer: The $58.28 entry rises to $70.98 in the central case, so the short leg loses before carry. The argument is relative underperformance within a diversified portfolio. The SPY hedge, collateral, borrow assumptions and total capital are explicit. Without the Intel short, the same SPY/cash allocation returns 7.10% under the central assumptions, with greater initial market exposure. That is a serious comparator.

questions_and_answers.question: Is the hedge creating your apparent edge?
questions_and_answers.answer: The portfolio calculation cannot establish mispricing. The central 6.43% return assumes 9.35% annual index total returns before SPY’s fee. Changing both the Intel valuation and market return to a consistent alternative equity-premium method gives 4.91%, slightly below the 4.94% reference hurdle. These conditional calculations do not establish a robust expected-return advantage. The original contribution is the auditable operating analysis.

questions_and_answers.question: DCAI already earns 41.5%. Why assume only 35%?
questions_and_answers.answer: 35% is a mature endpoint judgment, reached in 2040. One quarter does not establish margins through a normal supply and product cycle. At unchanged 0.80 capital productivity, 39.31% matches $58.28 with the assumed decline in risk; flat 11.555% requires 48.08%. Persistent margins near 40%, without offsetting manufacturing or corporate costs, would weaken my 35% assumption.

questions_and_answers.question: Which operating assumption actually matters most?
questions_and_answers.answer: Holding the maturing-risk path fixed, raising the mature margin from 35% to 40% adds $5.24, taking planning value from $53.77 to $59.01. Improving capital productivity from 0.80 to 1.00 alone adds $1.90. Both changes produce $60.90. Margin explains 73% of that operating uplift. These changes phase in after 2030; they do not forecast a near-term earnings surprise.

questions_and_answers.question: What did the Oracle audit prove?
questions_and_answers.answer: Published CPU-plus-memory prices give $14.5608 an hour for X12 versus $4.096 for X9. Accepting Oracle’s separate up-to-5x and up-to-6x throughput cases implies 1.41x and 1.69x work per dollar at those claimed levels. Intel still wins in those scenarios. No workloads or interviews were completed. This is list-price arithmetic, excluding other charges and private discounts. It does not establish Intel’s chip prices, margins or advantage over AMD.

questions_and_answers.question: How do you avoid mixing valuation dates and cash claims?
questions_and_answers.answer: $46.96 is the central December 2026 planning value; $70.98 is the central December 2030 value. The quote is November 4, leaving a 57-day mismatch for planning comparisons. Operating cash and financing tax benefits are valued separately, then cash, debt and other claims are reconciled. The model uses 5.51 billion planning claims and 3% terminal operating growth, with investment funded.

questions_and_answers.question: What evidence would make you change your view?
questions_and_answers.answer: Sustained margins near 40% across a broader product cycle; comparable output and profit with materially less total investment; or external Foundry customers earning returns after funding capacity. I would reconcile Products, Foundry and corporate costs together. Lower visible capex funded by partners, delayed payments or working capital would not automatically demonstrate better productivity.

questions_and_answers.question: What forces the market to agree, and what can go wrong?
questions_and_answers.answer: No demonstrated event forces convergence. Future reports can test the forecasts, but they are checkpoints. Stronger execution, durable pricing or lower required returns can invalidate the short. Borrow availability and interim collateral needs remain unverified. The fixed SPY hedge matches an estimated initial beta; it does not keep the position market neutral.

findings.before: The hedge produces 6.43% under the selected assumptions
findings.after: The illustrated portfolio returns 6.43% under the selected assumptions
findings.reason: 6.43% is CAGR on all original investor capital, not the hedge-leg return.

findings.before: Reported throughput: Up to 5x / Up to 6x; Work per dollar: 1.41x / 1.69x
findings.after: Assumed throughput: 5x / 6x; Conditional work per dollar: 1.41x / 1.69x
findings.reason: A claimed upper bound does not identify realized output. The accompanying note should retain that these are separate reported up-to scenarios and the performance was not rerun.

findings.after: The article omits memory from its quoted hourly costs.
findings.reason: The independently reconstructed CPU-only ratios are about8.96x and10.76x at the5x/6x throughput levels, so the cited10–12x headline is itself not exactly reproduced. Focus on the directly established billing omission.
